searchText: Somewhat on this topic, I wanted to propose a simple "do a few things and done" roadmap for EVM efficiency improvement: ------ 1. "EVMMAX + SIMD" Basically, the idea here is to take the EVMMAX spec, and change it so that instead of the indices being `x_offset, y_offset, z_offset`, they are: `x_start, x_skip, y_start, y_skip, z_start, z_skip, count` And you make it work for moduluses of small size, basically cover every modulus from 3 all the way up to `2**768-1` And design gas costs around that, so eg. an op with `count=8` and `modulus < 2**32` would cost as much as a single 256-bit EVM op does today, or even less I think of this as being "numpy for the EVM", it gives us a high-performance coprocessor inside the EVM that can be used to implement a very wide range of cryptographic operations highly efficiently - not just elliptic curve stuff, but also low-modulus operations, such as 32- bit STARKs (incl 32-bit Poseidon) and even lattice cryptography 2. Identify EVM operations that are cheaper than the others, and reduce their gas cost to 1 eg. ADD, SUB, PUSH, POP...... all of those are quite a bit cheaper than MUL Basically find everything that is "too expensive" today relative to our benchmark goals, and make it cheaper ----- We had an EIP for this 😅 even moduli as well? or just power of two and odd moduli? I remember EVMMAX as written before only covered power of two and odd, because those are the easy special cases for the montgomery mechanism, right? I've never seen an even modulus that's not a power of two ever used in cryptography in the wild so I'm ok with saying odd or power of 2 only Then let's bring it back! ACCEEELLLLLEEEEEEEERRRRRRRRRRRRRAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAATTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE The last EVMMAX spec only covered odd moduli because afaik it is not possible to do efficient montgomery multiplication with even moduli. I don't really know how efficient binary modular ~~arithmetic~~ multiplication is done. Multiplication modulo powers of two is just the base case, right? ie. it's the underlying native operation that everything else is being built on top of already One thing you could do with even moduli is chinese remainder decompose into `p * 2^k`, and montgomery the `p` part But IMO that's pointless extra complexity, let's just stick with powers of 2 and odd 😆 (powers of 2 are useful primarily for (i) hash functions operating over 32-bit numbers, and (ii) lattices) ah right the reduction step is just a bit shift ... yeah you don't even do the montgomery, you just apply a bit mask A couple more related things things that are frequently requested * Raising the contract Size Limit (can easily be set to 64k for runtime, possibly more for initcode) * Uncapping the Contract Size Limit, but that would require some things like varint jumps and headers values

------

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: 1. "EVMMAX + SIMD"

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: Basically, the idea here is to take the EVMMAX spec, and change it so that instead of the indices being `x_offset, y_offset, z_offset`, they are: `x_start, x_skip, y_start, y_skip, z_start, z_skip, count`

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: And you make it work for moduluses of small size, basically cover every modulus from 3 all the way up to `2**768-1`

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: And design gas costs around that, so eg. an op with  `count=8` and `modulus < 2**32`  would cost as much as a single 256-bit EVM op does today, or even less

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: I think of this as being "numpy for the EVM", it gives us a high-performance coprocessor inside the EVM that can be used to implement a very wide range of cryptographic operations highly efficiently - not just elliptic curve stuff, but also low-modulus operations, such as 32- bit STARKs (incl 32-bit Poseidon) and even lattice cryptography

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content:
2. Identify EVM operations that are cheaper than the others, and reduce their gas cost to 1

eg. ADD, SUB, PUSH, POP...... all of those are quite a bit cheaper than MUL

Basically find everything that is "too expensive" today relative to our benchmark goals, and make it cheaper
